title: How To Start Over In Three Steps
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin addresses teachers who feel their class has slipped out of control and are afraid that reestablishing accountability mid-year will trigger open rebellion. He argues that fear is unfounded as long as the reset is framed around what's best for students, and offers a three-step process: first, take personal responsibility for the current state of the classroom rather than blaming students, which opens rather than closes their willingness to listen; second, lay out the full classroom management plan in complete detail as if for the first time, leaving no ambiguity about what does and doesn't break the rules; and third, make an explicit vow to follow the plan exactly as described and to enforce consequences respectfully without lecturing or scolding. He argues that rules and consequences are not an impediment to relationships but the very foundation on which trust is built, and encourages teachers not to wait for a crisis point before starting over.
points: Teachers fear that reestablishing accountability mid-year will provoke rebellion, but this fear is unfounded if framed around student benefit.
Step one is taking personal responsibility for the classroom's current state rather than blaming students, which opens rather than closes trust.
Step two is laying out the full classroom management plan in complete detail, leaving no ambiguity about rule boundaries.
Step three is making an explicit, spoken vow to follow the plan exactly and enforce consequences respectfully, without lecturing.
Rules and consequences are reframed not as an impediment to relationships but as the very foundation trust and rapport are built on.
quotes: But the truth is, as long as you teach your behavior expectations in a way that demonstrates how they're best for them, these fears are unfounded.
So instead of blaming students for the chaotic learning environment, it’s best and healthiest to take responsibility yourself.
I haven’t done a good job of protecting your right to learn and enjoy school. I’m sorry and I feel terrible about it, but I’m going to make it up to you starting today.
Cover it all so there is no doubt, no question, no scintilla of confusion regarding what does and doesn’t constitute breaking your class rules.
You’ll speak the truth, but you won’t scold, lecture, raise your voice, or use any other negative or harmful methods.
The truth, however, is that not only aren’t they an impediment, they’re the very foundation upon which influential trust and rapport are built.
